overall_assessment: The search validation and recall-oriented evaluation architecture in Track 17 aligns with systematic search principles. Work Saved over Sampling (WSS@95%) accurately reflects reviewer workload reduction while preserving the non-negotiable rule forbidding autonomous study exclusion. Known-item recall tests at various rank thresholds (@10, @50, @100) are analytically verified, and deduplication cluster review burden accounts for ambiguous manual verification pairs. The information specialist panel emphasizes that synthetic gold sets must be supplemented with real topic-specific search strategies in prospective review settings.

findings.description: Work Saved over Sampling calculation returns None when target_recall is non-positive or exceeds 1.0, but could provide more granular diagnostic error types distinguishing out-of-range parameters from zero-total-record inputs.
findings.recommendation: Return a typed WssCalculationError enum instead of Option<f64> in production APIs.

findings.description: Recall@k assumes binary relevant labels; graded multi-level relevance (e.g., highly relevant vs background context) is not supported in the primary metric suite.
findings.recommendation: Add graded NDCG metrics when complex ranking tracks are evaluated.

findings.description: Review burden metric accurately computes the unique record count in clusters requiring human arbitration.
findings.recommendation: Maintain distinction between automated cluster reduction and human screening burden.

calibration_notes: Information specialists will strongly agree that WSS@95% and known-item recall are the appropriate primary metrics for systematic-review validation, and will appreciate the explicit refusal to auto-exclude studies.
